nature-econ-277.q: What implicit assumptions can framing carry?
nature-econ-277.a: Political ones, such as which group needs protecting, and technical ones, such as which variable is treated as constant.

nature-econ-255.q: What did Glewwe, Kremer and Moulin begin in 1994?
nature-econ-255.a: One of the earliest economic RCTs, a long-run school intervention in Kenya.

nature-econ-234.q: When is instrumental variables estimation needed?
nature-econ-234.a: When an explanatory variable is correlated with the error term, which makes ordinary least squares biased.

nature-econ-224.q: Which two kinds of variables do simultaneous equations models separate?
nature-econ-224.a: Variables set inside the model (endogenous) and those fixed in advance (exogenous).

nature-econ-264.q: What does McCrary's density test check for in a regression discontinuity design?
nature-econ-264.a: A bunching of observations at the threshold, such as more students just passing than just failing, a sign of gaming.

nature-eco-302.q: What are primary producers, and what are they mainly on land and in water?
nature-eco-302.a: Organisms that do primary production, also called autotrophs, forming the base of the food chain: mainly plants on land and algae in water.

nature-eco-320.q: Which abiotic factors shape where species can live?
nature-eco-320.a: They include water, light, temperature, humidity, acidity, salinity, altitude, minerals, tides, dissolved oxygen and soil.

nature-eco-318.q: What are the major threats to endangered species?
nature-eco-318.a: Habitat destruction and fragmentation, overexploitation, poaching, pollution, climate change and illegal wildlife trade.

nature-eco-282.q: Who popularized the Hutchinsonian niche concept, and what question did he ask?
nature-eco-282.a: The zoologist G. Evelyn Hutchinson, in 1957, asking why so many kinds of organisms live in one habitat.

nature-eco-337.a: Organisms fight directly over scarce resources, as large aphids eject smaller ones from the best feeding sites.

nature-eco-352.q: What kinds of gradient can an ecocline be?
nature-eco-352.a: A gradient in temperature (thermocline), chemistry (chemocline), salinity (halocline) or water density (pycnocline).

nature-eco-299.q: In a food web, what is connectance?
nature-eco-299.a: The fraction of all possible feeding links that actually occur in the network.

nature-eco-373.q: What can shift the Redfield ratio away from its usual value?
nature-eco-373.a: Nitrogen fixation, denitrification and changing nutrient inputs.

nature-eco-359.q: What are herbivores in a food chain, and what do they eat?
nature-eco-359.a: Primary consumers: they eat the carbohydrates plants make by photosynthesis, and carnivores in turn eat them.
